sections.category: Ollama 0.31 turns on multi-token prediction for Gemma 4, cutting local Apple-Silicon generation by nearly 90% and pushing the speedup into coding agents

bullets.body: Ollama shipped version 0.31 on July 1, 2026 with multi-token prediction (MTP) enabled by default for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon, and reports Gemma 4 now generating tokens nearly 90% faster on average across a coding-agent benchmark, with no change to model output. The mechanism is speculative decoding done in-model: Gemma 4 ships a small, fast draft model that proposes the next several tokens, and the main model verifies the proposal in a single pass and keeps whatever it agrees with, so several tokens land for roughly the cost of one whenever the draft is right. Ollama contributed a new small-batch matmul kernel to Apple's MLX framework that reads and unpacks each block of weights once and reuses it across the whole batch instead of re-reading per token; on an M5 Max with nvfp4 quantization that makes Gemma 4's largest matrix multiplications 2x to 2.5x faster, and the kernel is available to other MLX models, not just Gemma. The release also refreshes the bundled llama.cpp engine to build 9840, and the surrounding 0.30.11-0.31 train added thinking-capability detection, auto-installation hooks for Claude Code and opencode, Codex model-drift detection, and CUDA sm_86 support, per the Ollama release notes. The reason this matters beyond a benchmark line is that coding agents call the model continuously as they read files and run tools, and code is unusually predictable, full of closing brackets and repeated identifiers, so the draft model's proposals are accepted often and the acceleration compounds over an agent session. For anyone running local models behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint on a Mac, the practical read is that on-device agentic throughput just closed a meaningful part of the gap to hosted inference without new hardware.

citations.label: Ollama Blog - Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction

sections.category: Together AI raises an $800M Series C at an $8.3B valuation led by Aramco's Prosperity7, marking the open-model inference layer, not just the frontier labs, as the place capital is chasing scale

bullets.body: Together AI announced an $800 million Series C at an $8.3 billion post-money valuation on July 1, 2026, a 2.5x step-up from its February 2025 Series B that valued the company at $3.3 billion, bringing total funding to $1.3 billion. The round was led by Aramco Ventures' diversified program Prosperity7 Ventures US, with participation from Vista Equity Partners, General Catalyst, Emergence Capital, NVIDIA, March Capital, Pegatron, and SentinelOne's S Ventures, per DataCenter Dynamics. What distinguishes this from the frontier-lab mega-rounds is where the money sits in the stack: Together AI is a neocloud that trains and serves open-weight models such as DeepSeek, Nemotron, MiniMax, and Kimi at a fraction of closed-model cost, and it says it expects its GPU-infrastructure footprint to grow roughly 50-fold over the next five years. Prosperity7 managing director Abhishek Shukla framed the company as headed toward the public markets, echoing the same IPO gravity pulling on the labs themselves. The signal for teams choosing an inference vendor is that the open-model hosting layer is now being capitalized as a durable platform in its own right rather than a thin commodity reseller, alongside peers like Fireworks and Baseten that have drawn their own outsized rounds this cycle. The competitive question this funds is whether owned-GPU open-model inference can keep undercutting hosted frontier APIs on price while matching them on latency as the open weights it serves keep closing the capability gap.

sections.category: Tenstorrent CEO Jim Keller publicly denies Qualcomm buyout talks, cooling a reported $8-10B deal and signaling the RISC-V accelerator startup intends to stay independent through its IPO run

bullets.body: Speaking at a media event in Tokyo, Tenstorrent CEO Jim Keller said on June 30, 2026 and reiterated into July 3 that the AI-chip startup is not in acquisition discussions with Qualcomm, directly countering a mid-June report, originating with The Information and picked up by Reuters, that Qualcomm was weighing a full buyout at a reported $8 billion to $10 billion, per GuruFocus. Keller said the company is focused on building its own business, including IP licensing and high-end scalable AI work anchored in Japan, while leaving the door open to partnerships, noting Tenstorrent talks with many companies in strategic areas and that appetite for large deals across the sector has risen. The denial matters because it removes, at least for now, a consolidation path that would have folded one of the few credible RISC-V-based accelerator IP houses into a mobile-SoC incumbent, and it lands while Tenstorrent is mid-stride on an IPO bridge and confidential S-1 track rather than shopping itself. For buyers evaluating the non-NVIDIA accelerator field, the practical takeaway is that Tenstorrent's Galaxy rack roadmap and IP-licensing model remain on an independent trajectory instead of a Qualcomm integration timeline. The broader read is that the memory-bandwidth and inference-ASIC race is now valuable enough that acquisition rumors move markets, yet the leading independents are choosing public offerings over sale.

citations.label: GuruFocus - Tenstorrent CEO Denies Qualcomm Acquisition Talks

sections.category: Stathera closes an oversubscribed $55M Series B for MEMS silicon timing, betting that AI data centers will swap quartz clocks for semiconductor timing as synchronization becomes a bottleneck

bullets.body: Montreal-based Stathera announced an oversubscribed $55 million Series B on June 30, 2026, led by new investor Maverick Silicon with participation from Celesta Capital, BDC Capital, MediaTek Innovation Fund, TXC Corporation, and Ultratech Capital Partners, bringing total funding to $75 million, per citybiz. Stathera builds MEMS-based precision timing on a proprietary DualMode architecture that replaces legacy quartz oscillators with semiconductor timing, claiming roughly 85% smaller footprints plus better shock and vibration resilience, and it will use the round to ramp mass production of its second-generation 32.768 kHz portfolio, open a Silicon Valley office to court hyperscale and data-center customers, and fund a new GEN3 platform aimed squarely at communications, enterprise, and AI data-center clocks, with first customer samples targeted for 2028. The company frames the communications-and-data-center segment as the fastest-growing slice of an $11 billion annual timing market, and pegs the AI-data-center time-synchronization opportunity at about $1.5 billion cumulatively through 2030. The reason a clock startup shows up in an AI briefing is that as accelerator clusters scale to tens of thousands of GPUs, precise, resilient timing across nodes becomes a real constraint on interconnect and throughput, the same infrastructure layer that funds like Maverick Silicon are increasingly targeting. This is early-stage silicon with a 2028 sampling horizon, so it is a directional bet rather than a shipping product, but it marks timing as a named line item in AI-datacenter buildouts rather than an afterthought.

sections.category: AI events to plan around now: Geneva AI Week and an AI Tinkerers SF meetup open this week, with the hardware, security, and dev-conference tracks stacking up behind them through the fall

bullets.body: The nearest thing on the calendar is in Geneva: Geneva AI Week runs July 6-10, 2026 at the Palexpo convention center, opening with the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance (July 6-7) and rolling into the ITU AI for Good Summit (July 7-10), with a newly launched UN AI for Good Commission, co-chaired by Salesforce's Marc Benioff and Rwanda's Paul Kagame and seating Jensen Huang, Andy Jassy, Brad Smith, and Anthropic's Jack Clark, holding its first meeting July 8. For Bay Area locals, AI Tinkerers San Francisco hosts its next meetup on July 8 (a GTM-engineering track with Attio), the usual three-hour format of working demos from local builders. On the AI-chip and hardware track, AMD's MI400 Instinct series and "Helios" rack-scale system remain the marquee 2H-2026 catalyst to watch, while the nearest confirmed hardware gathering is Hot Chips 2026 at Stanford's Memorial Auditorium on August 23-25 (early registration closes July 31), with the AI Infra Summit in Santa Clara on September 15-17 behind it. The AI-security block clusters in early-to-mid August: SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit is August 11-12 at the Ritz-Carlton in Half Moon Bay, Black Hat USA and DEF CON 34's AI Village land in Las Vegas in early August, and OWASP Global AppSec USA follows in San Francisco on November 5-6; Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series continues its stops for teams focused on agent-hijack and MCP-layer defense. Also on the enterprise track, Ai4 2026 runs August 4-6 in Las Vegas and the ACM AI Leadership Summit is August 30 to September 2 in Atlanta, with GitHub Universe on October 28-29 and AWS re:Invent November 30 to December 4 in Las Vegas. The two immediate actions are showing up to the July 6-10 Geneva sessions if governance is your beat and the July 8 AI Tinkerers SF meetup if you are local; both the August AI Risk Summit and Hot Chips are the natural next venues for confidential-inference and secure-accelerator announcements.
